fixes.problem: Small leftovers. A faint sliver of spill (raw 17-44) lies on the void floor just under the slab's front edge. The beam's haze stops dead at the plane of the wall tops, so the cone reads as ending above the box instead of falling into it.
fixes.fix: Pull the cell pool's front edge in 5 cm (ry 2.05 -> 2.0, or after the fwd change in the window fix, check that the spill line is gone). Extend the top spot's haze down into the box at a lower density (0.004) so the cone visibly continues past the wall tops onto the floor.

hearing_room.verdict: Most round-1 fixes landed. HANDS now sits in the stage's exposure (graded mean 30, sleeve 40 against hand 132, paper peak 157) with a clean left-over-right fold and a stacked paper pile. The WIDE's crush fell from 49% to 17% of pixels at or below 3/255: sconces, housed broadcast lights and a clerk's table now tell the room. DAIS is a real low angle and its fascia falls off (13 graded under chairs at 64). It is still not at fern level, and most of what holds it back is in the WITNESS medium. Tim still reads as a smooth, androgynous man of about 30 whose hair is a shell with a raised step at the hairline. His face is lit almost flat (about 1.15:1). The shirt tone leaks onto the tie in pale flecks. The microphone stands at his shoulder while he looks away from it. The rows behind him crush to black (1.6 graded on the right), so 'empty rows behind' does not read. In the WIDE, the evenly washed blue drape (mean 71) pulls the eye harder than Tim's pool of light, its pleat tops end in a picket-fence row of pointed tips, and the lower-tier desk cap runs through the top of his head.

fixes.problem: Tim does not read as a man in his mid-fifties, even at TIM_AGE 0.78 and weight 0.7. The face is smooth with a small jaw. The chin is raised 18 degrees, which shows a long thin neck standing inside a loose collar ring. The receded hair is a smooth shell that ends in a visible raised step all round the hairline (temples and front), so it reads as a swim cap or wig edge. The face is lit almost flat: lit half 137 against shadow half 120 graded (about 1.15:1), which wipes out the form that would carry age on a stone statue.
fixes.fix: (a) TIM_UPPER head (-18, -16) -> about (-8, -8). Less chin-up shortens the neck in view, fills the collar and turns the face toward the mic and the dais. (b) Widen the neck about 12% and the jaw about 8%. Use MakeHuman targets if cast.person exposes them (neck-scale-horiz-incr about 0.35, chin-width-incr about 0.3, head-square about 0.3). Otherwise bind a 2x2x3 Lattice to the neck and jaw vertex groups. Pull the shirt collar ring about 6 mm in so it sits on the neck. (c) In recede_hair, ramp the 'volume' weights from 0 at the new edge to 1 over 25 mm, and mask soften_hair's clumps displacement to 0 within 15 mm of the edge. At a 5x crop the hair must meet the scalp flush, with no ledge. (d) In TRIMS['witness'], cut tv_fill_light 0.18 -> about 0.06 and leave the key, so the face's lit side is about 140 graded and the shadow side 65-80 (about 2:1), with readable shadow under the brow, cheekbone and jaw.

fixes.problem: Pale, ragged flecks run along the tie's left edge and knot (graded about 90-150 on a tie of 39). The shirt tone leaks onto the tie through holes in suit_tones' tie mask, or the shirt mesh pokes through. It sits on the hero's chest in the controlled medium.
fixes.fix: In suit_tones(), close tie_m before building shirt_m: dilate it by about 6 px (a 13x13 max filter, or scipy.ndimage.binary_dilation iterations=6) and fill holes inside the tie's bounding box. Then remove a 3 px band around tie_m from shirt_m. If flecks remain at a 5x crop of the knot, the cause is geometry: push the tie region out 2-3 mm with a Displace modifier along the normals, restricted to a tie vertex group built from the same mask.

fixes.problem: The drape is the biggest bright mass in the WIDE (mean 71 graded, against 40 for Tim's back and 44 for the table top), so the eye lands on it before the 'one pool of light'. The pelmet's shadow edge on the perfectly regular sine pleats (lam 0.21, one amplitude) cuts the top of every crest into a pointed tip. The result is a picket-fence or icicle fringe along the drape's top in both frames, and the pleats read as a CG comb.
fixes.fix: Add TRIMS['wide'] = {'washer': 0.55} and TRIMS['dais'] = {'washer': 0.75}. In drape(), move the washer slot and source from yb - 0.55 to about yb - 1.1, aim it at (0, yb + 0.1, 2.2) and widen the spread to about 100. The pelmet shadow then sits at the very top and the valleys fill. Alternatively, hide a cove strip under pelmet_lip, aimed straight down. Give each pleat its own pitch (lam x random 0.88-1.12) and amplitude (x 0.8-1.2) from a seeded sequence, so no two folds match. Targets: drape mean in the WIDE 40-48 graded, Tim's crown still the brightest point (at least 180), no pointed crest tips at a 3x crop.

fixes.problem: The lower-tier desk cap runs through the top of Tim's head, a tangency right at the figure the frame is about. The lit crown (208) merges into the lit cap line instead of standing against dark.
fixes.fix: Raise the wide camera from z 2.05 to about 2.4 and the aim z from 1.5 to about 1.6 to keep the framing. The near figure then drops faster than the far dais and his crown lands on the dark fascia panel (about 28 graded). Check that at least 15 px separate the crown from the cap line at 1280.

fixes.problem: He still does not speak into the microphone. The gooseneck head sits at chest height off his left shoulder (screen x about 735, y about 290, with his mouth at about 575, 230), and his head is turned the other way, toward the camera side.
fixes.fix: Re-place mic_tim with mic_place((TIM_X - 0.12, EDGE + 0.30), (TIM_X - 0.02, EDGE - 0.10), 1.15). The larger scale lifts the head to about 3-5 cm below mouth height and about 0.2-0.25 m in front of it. With the head turn reduced in fix 1, his mouth addresses it. From the witness camera, the mic head should sit level with his chin, at least 15 px clear of the face silhouette.

fixes.problem: The beat's 'empty rows behind' does not survive the grade. The public chairs behind him are 7.7 graded on the left and 1.6 on the right (they read in the raw frame), so he sits in a void. The young statue is a faint lone head and hand at 6-11 graded.
fixes.fix: Add a practical graze for this camera: an area light about 1.6 x 0.2 m, 25-40 W, COOL, at z 2.6 over the side aisle behind Tim (around x = TIM_X - 2.0, y = -3.0), with spread 60, aimed down across the chair backs, so their top rails and seat fronts make receding lines at 12-20 graded across the frame. Keep 'dl_fig_-2.4_-2.4_spot' at 0.15 so the statue stays a dark silhouette among the rows, and do not lift LIFT['witness'] instead.

fixes.problem: The water glass still reads as a black tumbler. In WITNESS it is opaque-looking, with three specular dots, no water line, no rim and no readable contact. In HANDS, seen from above, it is a ribbed black disc on the felt that reads as a jar lid or dial, not glass and water.
fixes.fix: Put a coaster under glass_tim: a 0.09 m disc of the paper material, 1 mm thick. The refraction then has something bright to show, and the base contact reads. Add a point light of about 0.4 W, radius 0.01, about 0.15 m behind and above the glass on the witness camera's line, so the rim and meniscus catch a thin highlight. In lathe(), raise segs from 48 to 96 or more, set the water surface 10-15 mm below the rim, and check from the hands camera for a clear disc of water with a rim highlight and no rib pattern.

fixes.problem: The microphone base shows a ragged, flat white patch (about 124 graded) and a scatter of dark chips on the disc, which are prop mesh and texture defects in the close-up. The mic head is a lumpy out-of-focus blob cut by the top edge at x about 800-870.
fixes.fix: After props.load('microphone'), split the mesh by loose parts (bmesh) and delete islands with fewer than about 1% of its vertices. Cover the white patch with a built button: sk.cyl radius 0.011, height 0.004, dark satin (about 0.06), bevel 0.0008. Alternatively, remap the texture's values above 0.8 to about 0.08. Shift the hands camera loc x by about -0.08, or roll it about 6-8 degrees, so the mic head leaves the frame and only the base and stem remain. Re-check this after the mic move in the fix above.

fixes.problem: The dais desk tops are bare except for the mics, so the two tiers read as a showroom rather than a hearing room that is set and waiting. The witness table has only one glass per place.
fixes.fix: At each upper and lower seat, place a blank walnut name tent (0.25 x 0.06 x 0.08 m, 2 mm bevel, no text) facing the well. Add a closed dark binder at 3-4 places and a water carafe with two glasses at the lower-tier centre. Add a carafe at the witness table's empty place. Keep all of them at 20-40 graded under the tier cans.

fixes.problem: The felt is still a flat CG plane with no nap or weave and a hard front edge. The upper (left) hand is puffy and glove-like, with no knuckle or tendon definition, beside the lower hand, which has nails.
fixes.fix: Felt: Sheen about 0.3 tinted pale blue and a noise bump at scale about 800, strength 0.06, for the nap. Round the cloth over the table edge with a 15-20 mm radius. Hand: add a subtle knuckle bump on the hand vertex groups (a Displace of 0.8-1.2 mm masked to the knuckle ridge, or a sculpted shape key), and curl the upper hand's fingers 4-6 degrees less, so they drape over the right wrist instead of hooking into it.

fixes.problem: The left-side figure near the staff table is a lone grey head (about 11-21 graded) with no body, so it reads as a bust on a bench. From behind, Tim's back is a smooth rounded blob with no jacket collar or white shirt collar at the nape.
fixes.fix: Either light that figure's shoulders with a 10-15 W spot so it reads as a seated person (torso 12-18 graded), or turn it off for this camera through HIDE. On Tim, make sure the 1-1.5 cm shirt collar shows above the jacket collar at the nape (the shirt mask covers the collar band at the back), so his silhouette reads as a dressed man.

fixes.problem: The 'curved' dais still reads as straight runs: the cap line barely bends across the frame. The top right is dead black wall (about 3 graded) apart from the sconce.
fixes.fix: Tighten the arc: raise SPAN from 38 to about 48 degrees, or cut the tier radii about 20%, so that from the low camera the cap line visibly bends (at least 40 px of sag over the frame). Lift the right wall with the existing sconce's down-scallop, or a second sconce about 2 m further along, to 8-15 graded.

visiting_room.verdict: Clear progress from round 1 (mean 5.25 to 6.25). The glass shot now nearly reaches fern level: a smooth ghost of Tim sits beside Dawn's face, his hair reads, and a door with a glowing vision panel stands behind her. The empty booth's phones and its smudged, reflecting glass are now real objects. It is still not professional. In the wide, the pool on the block wall above the lit booth is almost as bright as Dawn's face (graded 119 against 138), and a flat pale baffle beside the cast competes with them. In the empty frame, the brightest things are a vision panel in the dead centre and a flat lit baffle, not the two phones. The people and the paint still read as CG shells: a skin-tight top with a sculpted bust, Tim as a black silhouette, and wear that cannot be seen at frame scale. Both wall notices are blank (a noise-tinted sheet, no text), but neither one shows in any frame.

fixes.problem: The lit island is still shared with the wall. The soft pool on the visitors' face of the partition above the occupied booth's glass (x 690-890, y 200-265) measures 131 in the raw frame against 149 for Dawn's face (0.88x; the round-1 target was 0.6x), and 119 against 138 in the graded frame. It is the largest bright area in the frame and pulls the eye above the cast. The 0.095 m LIP does not stop it. The fitv3_down source sits at z 2.65, above the lip's bottom edge at 2.605, so it only blocks rays more than about 54 degrees from vertical. The wall above the glass is reached by rays 0-30 degrees from vertical.
fixes.fix: In visiting_room_set.py, deepen the partition-side lip on the visitors' lit fittings from LIP 0.095 to about 0.17 m. The lip's bottom then sits at about z 2.53 and cuts every ray steeper than about 29 degrees toward the partition, which covers the whole wall from the head rail (z 2.045) to the soffit. Alternatively, cut fitv*_down's spread from 120 to about 90 degrees while keeping TILT 24. Also set the lit diffuser objects' visible_diffuse = False, so the lens mesh's own emission does not wash the wall (it keeps glowing to the camera). Check the raw wide: the wall above the occupied glass should be at or below 90 (0.6x Dawn's face) while her face stays at 140-150 and Tim's shoulders keep their top light.

fixes.problem: The subject is not where the light is. The brightest element is idoor2's wired-glass vision panel in the dead centre of the glass (graded 106, a hard vertical bar). Next comes the inmates' x=0 baffle face, lit by fiti2 at level 1.0, a flat pale slab of 170x570 px (graded 81). The near phone box face is 38, darker than its own baffle at 48, and the far phone is 49 against 39 for the glass around it. The beat asks for the far phone 'in its own light', but there is no pool on it, and its box is jammed against the left glazing stop. The near box's top edge reaches only 145 in the raw frame (the round-1 target was about 200).
fixes.fix: In TRIMS['empty']: fiti2 1.0 to 0.35, so the baffle slab drops to about 45-50 graded. Register idoor2's glass material in st.PARTS['lens'] (as fitting() does for lenses), so the hook can scale it, and trim it to 0.3 for this camera. Add an 'emp_farkey' area light of 0.12 x 0.25 m, 15-25 W, spread 45, glossy on, camera off, about 0.35 m above and 0.12 m in front of the far phone box (x = BX[2] - 0.5 + 0.08, y = +0.3, z about 1.6), aimed down at the handset, so the far phone reads about 2x its surroundings (raw about 120). Add an 'emp_nearkey' of 0.15 x 0.04 m, 6-10 W, 0.3 m above the near box and 5 cm out from the baffle, raking down at about 20 degrees, so the box's top edge and the handset crown reach about 200 in the raw frame. To free the far phone from the left rail, move the camera from x = BX[2] - 0.32 to about BX[2] - 0.22, aim x from BX[2] + 0.15 to about BX[2] + 0.10, and check that the far box clears the glazing stop by at least 40 px, with the near phone still wholly inside the right third.

fixes.problem: Dawn's grip is still wrong. Her four fingers lie flat across her cheek above the handset instead of wrapping the handle. The handset hangs near vertical, so the mouthpiece sits at her neck and collarbone, about 10 cm below the corner of her mouth. It reads as a hand pressed to her face with a phone tucked behind it. In the frame's key close-up, this is the most visible pose error.
fixes.fix: In build_cast(), call handset_frame(h, +1, tilt=...) for Dawn with tilt about 22-28 degrees (from 0.0), so the handle runs from the ear canal forward to the corner of the mouth. Re-solve phone_hand so the palm centres on the handle's midpoint, not on the earpiece: shift the wrist target about 3-4 cm down the handset's Y axis, and raise _curl(h, 'R', 62) to about 75 so the fingers close round the 3 cm handle with the thumb along its inner face. After posing, check that no finger vertex lies within 5 mm of the head mesh, apart from the heel of the hand against the jaw. Re-run the cord so it still leaves the mouthpiece strain relief. Do the same tilt for Tim, so his reflection holds the handset the same way.

fixes.problem: Dawn's top reads as a skin-tight, mid-grey leotard. The bust is sculpted under it, with no drape, no folds at the armpit or waist and no weave at this distance. The sleeve and neck edges read as paint lines, not hems. A woman twelve years inside, in a washed prison tee, should look clothed, not body-painted. Nothing in her reads as older.
fixes.fix: Stage-side, on DawnPrison's female_casualsuit01 garment object (no change of wardrobe): add a Smooth modifier (factor 1.0, repeat about 8) limited to a vertex group weighted over the bust and lower chest, so the front reads as cloth hanging from the bust line rather than following it. Add a Displace modifier with a Clouds texture (noise size about 0.06 m, strength 0.003-0.005 m, midlevel 0.5) for loose-knit irregularity. In matt_cloth, raise folds from 0.45 to about 0.7 so creases darken at the armpit, under the bust and at the bowed waist. Add a 1 cm band 15% darker at the sleeve hems and the neckband. For age, raise sculpt_hair('DawnPrison') from 0.075 to about 0.14 and mix toward about 0.22 at the temples and the parting with a streaked noise (grey coming in). Push chest from 17 to about 22 degrees and neck from 6 to 8, and re-aim the head so the gaze still lands on Tim's mouth.

fixes.problem: Tim is one black silhouette. In the wide, his hair (51), neck and jacket back (27) merge into a single dark mass with no collar line. In the glass shot, the foreground head is 19 graded and the collar at the bottom right is crushed to 10, although the raw frame has a jacket collar and a shirt collar there. The dark foreground mass has no readable edge apart from the ear rim.
fixes.fix: Add a 'kick_Tim' area light of 0.25 x 0.25 m, 3-5 W, behind and above his right shoulder at about (BXO + 0.55, -1.45, 1.75), aimed at his nape: glossy on, camera off, volume off, and invisible in the glass (visible_glossy off on the glass, or place it so its reflection falls outside the pane). The target is a soft edge on the hair's crown line, the jacket's shoulder seam and the shirt collar at about 40-55 graded in both frames. Lift Tim's jacket in matt_cloth (rgb about 0.04 linear, charcoal) so the back separates from the counter shadow beneath it.

fixes.problem: The glass marks now read, but they read as mottled noise clouds, not as hands and faces. The smudge field is two thresholded noise scales, so it gives irregular blotches: a cluster like floating leaves cut by the top edge of the frame (x 330-560, y 0-30), and a stippled, dithered patch beside the vision panel. Real visiting-booth glass shows palm prints with finger streaks, a forehead or cheek smear, and wipe arcs.
fixes.fix: In security_glass(), add shaped prints per bay on top of the noise: a few world-space distance-field ellipses on the pane plane. Each is a palm about 9 x 11 cm with four or five finger streaks about 1.5 x 7 cm above it, at z 1.0-1.35 and offset left or right of the phone, plus a cheek or forehead smear about 12 x 6 cm at seated head height (z 1.15-1.3). Feather each one 1-2 cm and break it with fine noise (scale about 300) inside, so it reads as grease rather than a solid shape. Tighten the generic prints' map range from 0.6-0.74 to about 0.68-0.76, and multiply the band by 0 above z 1.6, so the blotches at the top of the frame go. Keep film_gain 3 for this camera.

fixes.problem: The new dressing does not reach the screen. Both notices are blank, which passes the hard rule, but neither shows in any frame. notice_v at (-3.3, -KW, 1.5) is hidden behind the first baffle in the wide; only its top 3-6 px peek above it, at about x 217-260, y 311-317. notice_i at (-1.45, Y1, 1.55) shows only as fragments through booth 2's upper glass, and it is out of shot in the glass and empty frames. The clock sits above the head rail and is hidden too. The CCTV dome and the bin are crushed to near black in the graded wide. Apart from the booths themselves, nothing in the frames says 'prison'.
fixes.fix: Move notice_v onto the visitors' face of the partition above the glass, in the falloff left of the lit pool: notice_panel('notice_v', (-1.5, -KW, 2.4), (0.45, 0.3), -1), landscape because the band between head rail and soffit is only 0.7 m. It projects at about (437, 211) in the wide and is out of the glass and empty shots. Move notice_i to (1.75, Y1, 1.5), where it reads through booth 4's glass in the wide at about (1046, 353). In the glass shot it falls behind the inmates' baffle (check that it stays clear of Tim's reflection). Keep both sheets blank, matt, and at or below about 60 graded. Move the clock to x about 1.2 on the inmates' back wall at z 1.95, or onto the visitors' left wall, wherever a camera sees it.

fixes.problem: The round-1 paint and counter wear exists in visiting_room_mats.py but is invisible at frame scale. The baffles and nosings read as clean, smooth CG panels in every frame (see the empty frame's right baffle and the wide's pale baffle). The counters are flat dark slabs, with no elbow-polished patch catching the fitting.
fixes.fix: In booth_paint(): raise edge from 0.13-0.16 to about 0.3, bare from (0.3, 0.305, 0.31) to about (0.4, 0.405, 0.41), and the orange-peel bump strength from 0.04 to about 0.08. Add a darker, glossier hand-grease patch (roughness minus 0.12, value x0.85) on the baffle nosings at z 0.9-1.3. In counter_top(), push the forearm-wear spots to roughness about 0.3 against 0.5, so the lit fitting's specular picks out a polished oval in front of Tim. Then check the empty frame's near baffle and the wide's x=0 baffle at 2x zoom for visible chips on the arrises.

fixes.problem: The visitors' x=0 baffle's +X face beside the cast (x 600-690, y 325-720) is a flat pale slab at 98 graded. After the wall pool, it is the largest bright shape in the frame, and it sits right against Tim and Dawn.
fixes.fix: Hang a camera-invisible flag (a black plane of about 0.3 x 0.4 m, visible_camera, visible_glossy and visible_diffuse off, shadows on) at the -X end of fitv3, 5 cm below the body. Alternatively, rotate fitv3_down about 8-10 degrees around Y toward +X. The top half of that baffle should fall to about 55-65 graded, with a gradient down its height, while Tim's shoulders and the counter in front of him keep their light.

fixes.problem: Dawn's armoured cord crosses in front of her raised right elbow with no contact or shadow, so it floats a few centimetres off the arm in a frame where the cord is a strong leading line.
fixes.fix: Lower the cord's sag from 0.16 to about 0.10, or route the curve's middle control point 3-4 cm toward the body, so it either rests on the forearm (and casts its shadow there) or clearly clears it by passing below the elbow.

leather_market.verdict: Not at a fern bar yet. The stall frame is the only one that works: a believable wall of bags, a bare tube and Dawn as a small dark figure facing it. Even that frame has a product-catalogue grid of pastel bags and a big flat grey counter slab filling the lower right. The wide has good bones: a long shuttered lane, wet concrete and reflections, and the shutters are well modelled. But 53% of the graded frame sits below 5/255, with dead black bands at the left 18% and right 15%. The lit stall is not the brightest thing in the lane (the foreground batten at top right competes with it). Most important, the beat does not read: no bag is visible, there is no stallholder, and Dawn stands apart in the lane facing the camera with her hands splayed instead of watching the handover. The puddle edges are blotchy camouflage noise, not water. The purchase close-up is the weakest. Two pale stone hands lie mirror-symmetric on a lumpy black duffel that fills 60% of the frame, so nothing pushes and nothing takes. The camera is near level, not looking down. The foreground holds an unexplained flat dark slab (it reads as a tablet) and a 'tape roll' that reads as a candle or a cheese wheel. The lighting is flat overhead fill with no rake on the bag. The renders are technically clean: no clipping, low noise, no fireflies. Means: about 5. No legible text or brands seen.

fixes.problem: Hands are mirror images: same height, same flat pose, same value, both resting on the top. There is no push and no take, so the transaction does not read and looks staged.
fixes.fix: In pose_buy, break the symmetry. Stallholder (L hand): put the heel of the palm against the bag's far END face, not the top. Wrist target about BX+0.40 at bag mid-height (bag_top-0.12), wrist dorsiflexed about 30 deg, fingers spread and curl 6, chest lean 18 deg toward the organiser, so the hand reads as pushing. Organiser (R hand): close it around the strap. Raise the strap loop 4-6 cm off the bag (edit the hero bag's strap verts or add a separate curve strap), set fingers to 70-80 curl and the thumb over the strap, and set the wrist 6-8 cm higher than the stallholder's. Darken the organiser's hand with hands_stone(value=0.28) so the two men differ. Check the palm contact from this camera (no gap under the palm).

fixes.problem: The camera is near level and on the bag's axis. The bag fills about 60% of the frame as a black blob, and the brief's 'looking down onto the counter' is not delivered.
fixes.fix: Move the camera to about loc=(1.0, 3.3, 2.15), aimed at the bag centre (BX, BY, TOP+0.08), lens 50, fstop 2.8. That is about a 40 deg down angle, offset 30-35 deg off the bag's long axis so the bag lies diagonally across the frame. Keep the bag at 35-45% of the frame width, with the counter edge running diagonally and the tags and tape readable in the lower third. Keep both men's sleeves entering from the frame edges.

fixes.problem: The beat does not read: no bag is visible and no stallholder. Dawn stands apart, faces the camera and is the brightest object; the organiser just reaches into a stall.
fixes.fix: Unhide the Stallholder in the wide and put him behind the counter, lit by hero_ceil_a. Turn the hero bag so its long axis faces the lane and is half off the counter edge in the organiser's grip, silhouetted against the bright bag wall. Rotate Dawn to face the stall (about 75 deg toward +X, a 3/4 back view to the camera), 1.0-1.2 m behind the organiser, and pose her hands loosely clasped in front (l_arm/r_arm forward 20-25, elbow 35). Lower her skin value in this camera (hands_stone and the face to about 0.38) so she does not out-shine the stall.

fixes.problem: The lit island is weak. The stall barely spills into the lane, the nearest lane batten (top right) is a competing hot spot, and 53% of the frame is crushed black, with dead bands at both sides.
fixes.fix: TRIMS wide: raise hero_ceil_a/b to 3.0-3.5x and lower hero_lane from 1.7 to 0.9. Turn off, or set to 'dim' at about 15 W, the nearest lane batten at frame top right. Add a 1.4 x 2.2 m area light in the stall's open front facing -X into the lane, 70-90 W, colour (0.85, 0.93, 1.0), so a hard-edged pool of light lies on the wet floor and the puddles reflect the stall's interior. Make the left wall readable: a dim_stall or one warm bulb (6-10 W) behind a shutter raised 30 cm on the left at mid-depth, plus a slightly higher shutter specular (roughness 0.35), so the left 20% shows ribs rather than black. Check that no more than 25-30% of pixels fall below 5/255 after grading.

fixes.problem: The wet floor mask is blotchy, camouflage-like noise with hard edges, scattered everywhere; it does not read as puddles in low spots.
fixes.fix: In the lane floor material, replace the wet mask with Noise scale 0.6-0.9 m, detail 2, through a ColorRamp smoothstep (0.48-0.55) multiplied by a gradient that favours the centre drain and the wall feet. Use three bands: puddle roughness 0.03 with a flat normal, a damp halo roughness 0.25 with albedo darkened 15% over 10-15 cm, and dry concrete roughness 0.65 with aggregate bump. Add a few tiny ripple bumps in the puddles.

fixes.problem: Foreground props fail. The black carrier-bag stack reads as a tablet or ledger slab. The tape is a solid cylinder with a disc on top (a candle or cheese wheel).
fixes.fix: counter_tape: model a real annulus (outer r 0.048, inner r 0.036, height 0.048) with a cardboard core 3 mm thick (an inner tube, a true hole through to the counter) and packing-tape material: amber (0.55, 0.38, 0.16), transmission 0.3, roughness 0.15, with a 4 cm loose tail curling onto the counter. Replace the slab with 4-6 folded thin black poly bags: subdivided planes with crease displacement, offset 1-2 cm each, roughness 0.45, edges catching light. Move the blank-tag bundle closer to the camera and fan it with the string loose.

fixes.problem: The wall of bags is a regular product grid: even rows and columns, every bag flat to the wall, too many pastels (cream, lilac, pale pink) under even light. It looks like a boutique catalogue, not a crammed market stall, and the four source models are noticeably cloned.
fixes.fix: In hang_wall, jitter hook x by +/-0.05 m and row z by +/-0.06 m. Hang 2-3 bags on about 40% of hooks, each 4-6 cm forward of the last, with random yaw +/-10 deg and roll +/-5 deg so handles splay. Scale the copies 0.85-1.15 non-uniformly (x vs z) to break the clones. Re-draw the palette toward real leather: 60% blacks, browns, cognac and burgundy at val 0.2-0.45, 25% navy, olive and taupe, at most 15% light (cream, pale pink, grey). Add a few clear poly dust bags over some bags. Let the light fall off toward the floor and the left wall (move hero_ceil_b toward the counter or add a barn-door blocker) so the top rows glow and the lower rows go dim.

fixes.problem: The counter fills the lower right quarter as a flat, featureless grey slab (a lesson already in the brief). The black extra bag stands end-on and reads as a backpack, not a duffel.
fixes.fix: Either move the camera about 0.4 m left and to aim (3.4, 5.7, 1.3) so the counter takes at most 18% of the frame, or dress it: a brushed steel top with scratches and a dented bevelled front lip (bevel 6 mm), a laminate front with a scuffed lower edge, a rolled cable and a stack of carrier bags. Rotate the hero bag 30-40 deg on Z so its long side and both handles show in 3/4 view, and add a rim from hero_ceil_b so its silhouette separates from the wall.

fixes.problem: Dawn's chin is not lifted, and from directly behind she reads as an exact back view, not a lost profile.
fixes.fix: In pose_look, raise the aim target to about z 2.6 and add head pitch -18 to -22 deg (chin up) plus chest (-6, 0). Rotate her holder 12-15 deg so the camera sees her cheek and jaw line edge-on against the bright bags. Curl the fingers of the right hand that hangs by the shelf to 40 and move it 4 cm off her thigh.

fixes.problem: The lane reads as a storage-unit corridor, not a Chinese leather market: the cables, awnings and clutter are not visible.
fixes.fix: Light the overhead: let lane battens graze the corrugated awnings (set their energy so the awning undersides read at about 0.05-0.1). String 3-5 sagging cable bundles (the catenary bundle helper, sag 0.25-0.4) across the lane at 2.6-3.2 m so they silhouette against the haze. Add stacked cardboard cartons and a folded hand trolley outside two shutters, a tarp-covered bale and a plastic stool. Hang 2-4 bags from an S-hook rail outside the hero stall's front post so the trade reads from afar. Keep all cartons blank.

fixes.problem: Flat overhead fill: the duffel's wrinkles are lit softly from above with no raking light or rim, and the counter is uniform grey.
fixes.fix: Cut the overhead contribution: TRIMS purchase hero_ceil_a 0.6. Make hero_alley a narrower key (size 0.05 x 0.8, energy 30-40) at a 35-45 deg rake from the stallholder's side so the PVC folds get hard highlights and a shadow side. Add a 0.3 x 0.3 rim at 15 W behind the bag at counter height. Counter top: roughness 0.35-0.45 with brushed anisotropy and a slight scratch/grime map, plus a bevelled front edge.

fixes.problem: The hanging bags have a uniform satin CG sheen with no seams or edge piping; up close they read as soft plastic.
fixes.fix: Per copy, randomise rough_add between 0.15 and 0.35 and add a fine leather-grain bump (Voronoi scale about 400, strength 0.05). Give the edges a slight darkening from an AO or pointiness mask (edge piping and wear), so neighbours differ in sheen as well as hue.

chicago_night.verdict: Round 2 is a clear step up and both checks pass: the tag is blank, and no tower reads as a real Chicago landmark (flat-topped boxes with twin red corner lights, no antennas, spires, X-bracing or white cladding). The other round-1 fixes also landed: the 20 km clip brought back the sky and a deep skyline, the verticals and the casing corners are fixed, the two lamps frame the cool city, and the wide and suitcase frames are now the warmest graded frames in the film (lit R-B +17.9 and +17.5, medians 26.6 and 30.6). It is not fern level yet. In the close-up, which is nearly there, the tag hangs from a strap that stops about 7 cm below the grip, in mid-air. The case reads pale silver in the wide (graded 82) but charcoal in the close-up (45). And Dawn is still the least-read thing in the establishing shot: a flat black suit with no edge or fabric against black blocks, her mug hidden, next to a rust chair that the grade crushes to near black.

fixes.problem: The blank tag hangs from nothing. Its 7 cm strap ends about 40 px (about 7 cm) below the grip bar, in the gap between the telescoping tubes, so in the hero close-up the tag floats in mid-air (it also shows in the wide). Cause: in chicago_night_set.suitcase(), gz0 = min(p.z for p in grip_pts) + lift takes the bottom of the whole lifted grip assembly (about 0.895 m), not the grip bar the hand holds.
fixes.fix: Hang it from the bar. Set gz1 = max(p.z for p in grip_pts) + lift - 0.012 (the bar's centre line). Replace case_tag_strap with a loop that wraps the bar in the x-z plane at y = gyc: tube('case_tag_loop', [W(gx+0.012, gyc, gz1-0.07), W(gx+0.012, gyc, gz1+0.004), W(gx, gyc, gz1+0.016), W(gx-0.012, gyc, gz1+0.004), W(gx-0.012, gyc, gz1-0.03)], 0.0022, M['leather'], res=4). Then hang case_tag with its top edge at gz1-0.07 (centre at gz1-0.115) and the eyelet at gz1-0.078, turned 12-15 degrees about Z out of the case's plane so its edge catches the case card. Check at 4x in the suitcase frame that the loop visibly wraps the grip and the tag is still blank, and check the wide too.

fixes.problem: Continuity, and the brief's rule that charcoal bags read dark. The same case reads pale silver-grey in the wide: its front is graded 82, which is 0.71 of the off-white door slab beside it (115). In the close-up the case is charcoal (45). TRIMS is empty, so case_card (9 W aimed at the case front) also burns in the wide, on top of entry_light (the 380 W spot right above the case). The wide's camera exposure (+0.5) is 1.55 stops over the suitcase camera's (-1.05), so that extra light shows.
fixes.fix: Set TRIMS['wide'] = {'case_card': 0.0, 'entry_light': 0.6}. Targets on the graded wide: the case front at 40-55, the door slab at 95 or more, and the floor pool by the door still visible, with a glint on the zip pulls. If the case stays above 55, aim the entry spot about 0.3 m into the room (+X) so the case sits at the edge of its cone. Do not grey the prop.

fixes.problem: Dawn's clothes never read as fabric. In the wide her jacket measures raw 5 (graded 8), the darkest thing in the room, and it merges with the black mid-rise blocks behind her torso, while her bare stone legs, the brightest part of her, pull the eye down. In the window shot her back is raw 3: a flat black cutout filling about 20% of the frame, with no seam, fold or edge. The warm far-side rim asked for in round 1 is not there.
